To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the evolutionary divergence of exons is affected by their level of inclusion into mature mRNAs (the proportion of transcripts containing an exon) and their expression pattern.
the evolutionary rates of exons are influenced by the same selective factors that affect gene evolutionary rates.

(a) alternative splicing affects both gene and exon divergence, (b) the effect of alternative exon splicing is more pronounced in exons with lower inclusion levels and (c) the effect of expression pattern is more pronounced in genes with higher expression levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of alternative RNA splicing on the evolution of protein coding sequences.
the evolution of alternative splicing and its effect on exon evolution in Drosophilla.
understanding how alternative splicing affects the evolutionary dynamics of genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alternative splicing and expression level are both important selective factors that affect exon evolution.
exon evolution is affected by the same factors as gene evolution, namely expression level and pattern, and that these factors have an effect at different levels of the genome.
the evolution of exons within a gene and of genes within the genome are not independent events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

genes with a broad pattern of expression and a low inclusion level of exons are more conserved than those that are expressed in a narrower range of tissues and with a higher inclusion level of exonic regions.
the evolutionary divergence of a gene is a function of its expression pattern and that this pattern is reflected at the level of its individual exons.
alternative splicing, expression, and inclusion level are all important factors in shaping the patterns of evolution of both exons and genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alternative splicing and expression pattern affect the evolution of exons in Drosophilla melanogaster.
the evolution of genes undergoing alternative spicing and the evolution of exons can be explained by similar selective factors.

the evolution of genes is a complex phenomenon that is not limited to the evolution of the coding region but also includes the evolution of noncoding regions and of the expression patterns of the different isoforms.
